summary:
The harness (eng/rules-harness/harness.py) now judges rows at HEAD. It used to refuse the whole run whenever the engine left the SL-049 must_not_import rule UNRAN; the fix fits in harness.py and needs no engine change. That rule cannot run on the harness's scratch copy: the engine keeps code graphs under TAAD3_HOME, which the harness points at its own scratch, so no graph is ever there. The harness now treats an unran rule that is an import rule as NOT RUN and names it on the clean line and on the summary line of every run, exit 0 included. It is never counted as passed: the verdict stays 'unable'. Any other unran rule still stops the run, and a new C-006 case proves that.

On a `git archive` of HEAD (c746a31) the fixed harness judged all 48 rows. Two came back STRAY-HIT, F03 and F18: their plants genuinely also break settled rules added later by SL-056 and SL-046. I recorded those hits through a new Fitness-only row field, `also_settled`, after which all 48 are AS-RECORDED, exit 0. C-007 and C-008, including the delete case at Twinned-1 (11/14/27 on this tree, 12/16/28 on the two-scope copy), pass with the engine on this tree and on the two-scope copy under both powershell.exe and pwsh. Per Q-129, SettledCountProbe.ps1's Get-Line now uses RuleCases.ps1's own Get-RuleCounts instead of the literal 11/15/27.

files.why: run_fitness now records which unran rules are import rules. New not_run_on_scratch/describe_not_run: import rules are named 'NOT RUN, not passed' on the clean line and the summary line. check_clean expects the verdict 'unable' only when every unran rule is an import rule, and refuses any other unran rule. The per-batch check requires the same unran set as the clean baseline. judge() takes a new row field also_settled (settled rules the plant also breaks, expected from Fitness only). The docstring states the exit-code contract.

F03 records also_settled 'only DirectoryReader lists a directory' (SL-056) and F18 records 'the breakdown reads the finished scan store and never the filesystem' (SL-046). Both were measured by this slice's run on a HEAD archive, the first run the harness could make since SL-049. The _note explains the new field.

C-007 now expects 'none unmatched', reads the rule count from 'fitness (pass|unable), N rules', and checks that every must_not_import entry in this tree's yaml is named NOT RUN with a verdict other than pass (or 'none unran' and pass when there are none). C-006 gained a bite: a stand-in engine that leaves a non-import rule unran must still stop the clean baseline, exit 2, and is never named NOT RUN.

Q-129: Get-Line no longer pins 11/15/27. It loads RuleCases.ps1's own Get-RuleCounts through the PowerShell parser (one definition, not a copy) and takes a twinned offset, so Misclassified passes -1 instead of the literal 14.

obligations.how: `SL-069-EveryCaseFollowsCounts.Tests.ps1 -Shape EngineCases` with -EnginePython/-EngineRoot ran C-008 on this tree and on the two-scope copy under powershell.exe and pwsh: exit 0, 'All checks held.' each time. The delete case's ok row reads 'rules-parity: AGREE 11 facts <- 14 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 49 settled' on this tree and '12 facts <- 16 twinned entries, 28 patterns' on the copy (Twinned-1, Facts and Patterns unchanged). F02 reads AS-RECORDED and F12 MISSED-BY-FITNESS as C-008 requires.

After the harness fix (import rules named NOT RUN, never passed), C-007 and C-008 were run with the engine on the clean tree and on the two-scope scratch copy under both hosts, all exit 0 (EngineCases, 351 s). C-007 reads 'xunit 11 Facts, 0 hits' on this tree and 'xunit 12 Facts, 0 hits' on the copy. C-006 and C-009..C-014 also pass with the changed harness.

deviations: Unrunnable rules are identified by kind, not by one hard-coded name. The rebuild order offered 'naming that one rule as unrunnable on scratch copies'. The harness instead lets through only rules the engine returns as unran that carry must_not_import, and prints each one's name, so today it names exactly 'the provider does not use the code it checks'. The reason is the same for any import rule: the graph lives under TAAD3_HOME, which the harness points at its own scratch. A hard-coded name would stop the harness again on the next import rule for that same reason. Every unran rule that is not an import rule still stops the run (new C-006 bite). Giving the scratch copy a real code graph was rejected: it would drive the engine's CRG store, and SL-065 found build=True alone does not fix it.

Scope reached eng/rules-harness/plants.json and added one row field (also_settled) to judge(). The first run the harness could make at HEAD showed F03 and F18 as STRAY-HIT. Their plants genuinely also break settled rules added later (SL-056 and SL-046), and F03 is one of C-008's 16 rows, so C-008 could not pass without recording it. The existing `also` field names twinned rules and expects xUnit to fire too, which a settled rule cannot do.

C-007's expectations changed with the harness's wording. 'none unmatched or unran' became 'none unmatched' plus a check that every yaml must_not_import entry is named NOT RUN and the verdict is not pass. The rule-count regex also accepts 'unable'. C-006 gained a refusal bite.

SettledCountProbe.ps1:125 is derived in this slice, reversing the design's key decision to leave it out. Q-129, as the rebuild order states it, directs the derivation. The design listed the same point as an open question, so its decision predates the answer rather than overriding it; m6 was overridden only on its timing claim. Q-129's own text is not in the tree (a search of .taad found no Q-129), so this rests on the rebuild order's statement of it.
follow_ups: The harness never measures import rules: a scratch copy has no code graph. If must_not_import behaviour should be measured the way content rules are, a separate slice has to give the scratch copy a graph through the engine's CRG store, which may need engine support.
